jessica (acme-corp): Hi — since the rollout this morning (around 09:12 UTC) our production calls to /v1/generate started returning invalid schema for the `user_profile` field. We rely on strict JSON shape for downstream processors, so this is blocking. Example request id: req_0a3f9.

jessica (acme-corp): Previous correct response (yesterday):
```json
{"user_profile": {"id": 12345, "emails": ["jsimmons@acme.com"], "metadata": {"signup_ts": "2023-11-01T12:00:00Z"}}}
```

jessica (acme-corp): Today we get one of these variations (rotating):
1) `emails` becomes a string: "jsimmons@acme.com" instead of an array;
2) `metadata` sometimes missing entirely;
3) Occasionally an extra top-level key `warning` with a non-JSON-safe value (looks like unescaped control chars).

maria (support): Thanks for the report — sorry for the disruption. Can you confirm the model and version you were routed to for req_0a3f9? Also if you have the full raw response body (including headers) that would help. Any chance the client library changed?

jessica (acme-corp): We pinned model to `gpt-open-1` in our config. The response headers: `x-rw-model: gpt-open-1`, `x-rw-model-version: v2026-03-15-2`. Client SDK unchanged. Sending raw body below (redacted):
```
{"user_profile":{"id":12345,"emails":"jsimmons@acme.com","metadata":null}}
```

maria (support): This matches the schema regression you described. I'm escalating to eng-ml. Tagging @jay and @oliver.

jay (eng-ml): Looking. Quick hypothesis: we rolled a schema-strictness change to the post-processing step in the token->JSON mapper during today's canary push. Deploy-bot shows canary at 08:55 then global at 09:05 (see deploy id deploy_2026_03_15_0910).

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for model gpt-open-1 at 2026-03-15T08:55:12Z.
deploy-bot: Global rollout completed at 2026-03-15T09:05:47Z.

jay (eng-ml): Can you share the exact prompt + instruction block you used (or a redacted minimal repro)? If it's making arrays become strings that's likely a parsing type-inference bug in the structured output postprocessor when sequences are length 1.

jessica (acme-corp): Minimal repro (we call Redwood API with the following instruction):
```text
System: return a JSON object under key `user_profile` with `emails` as an array of strings and `metadata` as object
User: provide profile for user 12345
```
Request payload (redacted):
```json
{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"<above>","temperature":0.0}
```

maria (support): Noted. We've attached request id and linked this to ticket S-2026-1734. Jay — do you want us to collect additional examples? We have ~7 customer reports in the last 40 minutes, most from heavy-schema integrations.

jay (eng-ml): Yes, please. We need: raw response bodies for a few different requests, corresponding request ids, and whether `emails` had 1 or multiple values. Also whether any of the responses had `metadata` present. That will help confirm whether the parser coerces length-1 sequences to scalar.

oliver (product): Prioritize customers with strict schema dependencies. If this is a regression introduced by today's postprocessor change, we should consider a temporary rollback to the previous build while we patch. What's the risk of rollback?

jay (eng-ml): Rollback risk is low — the change was limited to the structured-output parser binary (non-model weights). Canary was 10% of traffic for ~10min then global. Patch should be straightforward: avoid length-based coercion and always wrap single elements in arrays when the schema expects an array.

maria (support): Jessica — we'll gather examples and provide ETA. For immediate mitigation: can you add a client-side quickfix to coerce `emails` into an array when it's a string? I know it's a workaround but might be fastest.

jessica (acme-corp): We can add the client fix, but several teams have immutable downstream processors and can't change without release cycles. Please escalate — this is a production outage for us.

jay (eng-ml): Understood. I'm creating a hotfix branch now. Also adding logging around the postprocessor for the next hour to capture raw token streams for failing requests (will redact PII).

maria (support): Collected these additional request ids from other customers: req_0a3fa, req_0a3fb, req_0a3fc. All routed to same model-version v2026-03-15-2.

deploy-bot: Hotfix branch created: mm/fix-struct-output-coerce. CI job started (job_9981).

jay (eng-ml): CI passed. Preparing canary hotfix deploy. Rolling canary now to 5% to validate (deploy_hotfix_9981).

deploy-bot: Hotfix canary started at 2026-03-15T10:02:33Z.

maria (support): Quick status: we've informed impacted customers and provided client-side workaround where possible. Jessica — want us to schedule a quick conference call with engineering?

jessica (acme-corp): Yes please, 10:15 UTC would work. Thanks for quick action.

jay (eng-ml): Canary hotfix looks good on initial checks. Requests that previously returned string emails now return arrays. Rolling to global in ~7 minutes if no regressions.

deploy-bot: Hotfix global rollout complete at 2026-03-15T10:09:51Z.

jay (eng-ml): We've deployed the hotfix globally. Follow-up actions: 1) postmortem on root cause (parser made a length-1 heuristic); 2) add unit tests for single-element arrays; 3) add telemetry to assert schema types for structured outputs; 4) create retro notes for release process to keep structured-output changes behind a feature flag.

oliver (product): Also notify account management for customers impacted and consider offering credits for downtime.

maria (support): Closing loop with Jessica and other customers. Jessica — can you confirm your downstream processors are green now?

jessica (acme-corp): Checked a few jobs, looks good — `emails` are arrays now and `metadata` has returned for previously missing cases. We'll monitor and report if anything else crops up. Thanks team. :raised_hands:

maria (support): Recording incident for ops: INC-2026-045-schema-regression. Assigning to eng-ml for postmortem.

jay (eng-ml): I'll own the postmortem. Will post a short write-up by EOD with timeline, code diff, and tests added.

maria (support): Thanks everyone. Closing thread but will reopen if customers report new issues.
